issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction over the claims and amount in controversy under Nevada law.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction over Yanhui
issues.why: The court must ensure it can exercise jurisdiction over the defendant based on contacts and service.

issues.label: Proper venue
issues.why: The court must verify the action is filed in the correct county/court for the dispute.

issues.label: Adequacy of service
issues.why: The court must confirm defendant was properly served, especially given the earlier default.

issues.label: Effect of prior default proceedings
issues.why: The court must assess whether earlier default-related filings impact disclosures, admissions, or prejudice.

issues.label: Setting aside default propriety
issues.why: The court must confirm the default was properly set aside and whether conditions/sanctions applied.

issues.label: Pleading sufficiency
issues.why: The court must determine whether the complaint states viable claims for each asserted cause of action.

issues.label: Statute of limitations
issues.why: The court must determine whether any claims are time-barred based on accrual and tolling.

issues.label: Choice of law
issues.why: The court must determine which state’s substantive law governs the joint venture and tort claims.

issues.label: Existence of joint venture
issues.why: The court must decide whether facts establish a joint venture (agreement, shared control, profit sharing, etc.).

issues.label: Enforceability of oral agreement
issues.why: The court must decide whether an unwritten joint venture/contract is enforceable.

issues.label: Statute of Frauds applicability
issues.why: The court must determine whether an agreement involving interests in real property must be in writing.

issues.label: Part performance exception
issues.why: The court must assess whether payment/acts remove the agreement from the Statute of Frauds.

issues.label: Resulting trust theory
issues.why: The court may need to consider whether Yanling’s contribution creates a resulting trust in the properties.

issues.label: Constructive trust theory
issues.why: The court may need to consider whether equity imposes a constructive trust due to alleged wrongdoing.

issues.label: Fiduciary duty existence
issues.why: The court must determine whether a joint venture created fiduciary duties affecting remedies and proof.

issues.label: Breach of contract elements
issues.why: The court must decide whether there was a contract, breach, causation, and damages.

issues.label: Implied covenant scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether conduct breached good faith in performing an existing contract.

issues.label: Unjust enrichment availability
issues.why: The court must determine if quasi-contract relief is barred by an enforceable contract or is alternative.

issues.label: Conversion viability
issues.why: The court must determine whether conversion applies to money/proceeds and whether identifiable funds exist.

issues.label: Accounting remedy
issues.why: The court must consider whether an accounting is required to determine rents/profits from the venture.

issues.label: Partition or sale proceeds rights
issues.why: The court must assess whether plaintiff has any ownership interest entitling her to sale proceeds.

issues.label: Measure of damages
issues.why: The court must determine proper damages (return of capital, profits, rents, tracing, offsets).

issues.label: General vs special damages
issues.why: The court must classify the damages sought to decide whether NRCP 16.1 computation was required.

issues.label: NRCP 16.1 disclosure duty
issues.why: The court must interpret whether plaintiff’s claimed amounts required a detailed computation and supporting docs.

issues.label: Timing of damages disclosure
issues.why: The court must determine whether disclosures were timely under NRCP 16.1 and scheduling orders.

issues.label: Sufficiency of computation
issues.why: The court must decide what level of detail satisfies NRCP 16.1(a)(1)(A)(iv) for these damages.

issues.label: Use of motion papers as disclosure
issues.why: The court must decide whether damages stated in default-judgment papers can satisfy disclosure obligations.

issues.label: Duty to supplement disclosures
issues.why: The court must apply rules requiring supplementation when computations change or become available.

issues.label: Discovery closure impact
issues.why: The court must consider prejudice from late disclosures after discovery closed and trial approached.

issues.label: Expert disclosure compliance
issues.why: The court must consider whether expert timing/availability affects damages computation obligations.

issues.label: Motion in limine proper scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether exclusion of damages evidence via in limine motion was procedurally proper.

issues.label: Sanction authority and rule basis
issues.why: The court must identify the correct rule/authority for excluding evidence and/or dismissing claims.

issues.label: Exclusion sanction proportionality
issues.why: The court must assess whether exclusion of special damages was proportionate to the violation.

issues.label: Consideration of lesser sanctions
issues.why: Before case-ending outcomes, the court must consider lesser sanctions (continuance, reopening discovery, fees).

issues.label: Willfulness and diligence findings
issues.why: The court must determine whether plaintiff’s noncompliance was willful, in bad faith, or merely negligent.

issues.label: Prejudice to defendant
issues.why: The court must assess whether late computation prejudiced defendant’s ability to prepare for trial.

issues.label: Opportunity to cure
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether plaintiff was given a fair chance to cure and whether she complied.

issues.label: Effect of missing court-filed disclosure
issues.why: The court must consider whether disclosures must be filed vs served and how the record proves service.

issues.label: Treatment of late supplemental computation
issues.why: The court must decide whether to accept or strike the computation filed after the court deadline.

issues.label: Reconsideration/relief procedures
issues.why: The court must consider whether plaintiff needed to seek reconsideration or relief from deadline to avoid sanctions.

issues.label: Dismissal with prejudice standard
issues.why: The court must apply the standard for case-terminating sanctions and dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Due process for dismissal
issues.why: The court must ensure notice and an opportunity to be heard before imposing a case-ending sanction.

issues.label: Dismissal vs summary judgment
issues.why: The court must determine whether the proper mechanism was dismissal sanction or dispositive adjudication.

issues.label: Remaining claims without specials
issues.why: The court must decide whether any claims survive if special-damages evidence is excluded.

issues.label: Nominal damages possibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether breach claims can proceed on nominal damages even without computation.

issues.label: Equitable relief despite exclusion
issues.why: The court must consider whether restitution/constructive trust/accounting are distinct from excluded damages evidence.

issues.label: Causation and tracing of proceeds
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiff can trace her funds to property purchases or proceeds.

issues.label: Offsets and expenses accounting
issues.why: The court must determine whether defendant may offset costs (mortgage, taxes, repairs) before profit split.

issues.label: Evidence admissibility for rents/profits
issues.why: The court must decide what documentary evidence (leases, bank records) is required and whether it was disclosed.

issues.label: Credibility and proof of oral terms
issues.why: The court must determine whether testimony and conduct sufficiently prove the alleged 50/50 arrangement.

issues.label: Remedy election and duplicative recovery
issues.why: The court must prevent double recovery across contract, unjust enrichment, and conversion theories.

issues.label: Attorney fees entitlement
issues.why: The court must consider any contractual/statutory basis for fees and whether sanctions justify fee shifting.

issues.label: Costs and sanctions
issues.why: The court must consider costs or monetary sanctions related to disclosure violations.

issues.label: Final judgment form and findings
issues.why: The court must enter a proper final judgment and, if required, make findings supporting dismissal and sanctions.

issues.label: Appellate standard of review
issues.why: The court must build a record recognizing that evidentiary sanctions/dismissal are reviewed for abuse of discretion.
